version: Mahamaya Complaint Structured Phenotyping Instrument — MCSPI-P1 v1.0
status: Research prototype / clinician decision-support aid; not a validated diagnostic scale
principles: Patient wording is retained while structured phenotype variables are captured.
Rule-based explanations are transparent and clinician-reviewable.
No probability of disease is generated from unvalidated symptom scoring.
Tests and treatment are suggestions for clinician review, not autonomous orders.

fields.help: Optional estimate; do not force if unknown.

fields.placeholder: Patient wording, triggers, chronology, previous episodes, response to prior treatment…

redFlags: Large, ongoing or clinically significant hemoptysis
Hemodynamic instability, syncope or altered mental status
High-risk immunocompromised state with acute deterioration
Possible TB pattern: prolonged cough with systemic symptoms / exposure
exam: Work of breathing and ability to speak
Cardiovascular exam if orthopnea/edema or cardiac clues
investigations: CXR when clinically indicated; chronic cough baseline imaging
Spirometry ± bronchodilator reversibility when airflow disease suspected
FeNO and/or blood eosinophils where available when eosinophilic/T2 airway disease is suspected
Sputum microscopy/culture when infection or significant productive cough is suspected
WHO-recommended rapid molecular TB testing when TB is suspected
CBC/CRP or other labs only according to clinical context
CT chest is targeted, not routine for every cough
differentials: Asthma / cough-variant asthma / eosinophilic airway disease
Heart failure / pulmonary edema when compatible
Other pulmonary pathology requiring targeted assessment
management: Treat the confirmed/working cause rather than the symptom label alone
Use urgent/emergency pathway for red flags
Avoid automatic antibiotic selection from sputum colour alone
Document response and safety-net / follow-up plan
